notes: The page is three near-identical dispatch blocks plus the tail of a fourth, and every turn on it is the chair's, always labelled 'Sr. Presidente (Guinle). —'. Eleven labels are printed, so I listed eleven turns even though several are word-for-word repeats; the three 'Corresponde considerar...' turns share their first fifteen words and only diverge afterwards, so I extended those first_words far enough to tell them apart. The unlabelled 'Si no se hace uso de la palabra, se va a votar.' after each 'En consideración en general.' is a run-on paragraph of that same turn, not a new turn. The last thing printed on the page is the bare section number '57', centred and bold, with its title falling on the next page; I listed it as a heading with no title rather than dropping it. Each centred blue underlined 'Orden del Día Nº ...' line stands where the text of the order would be inserted, and no document text is actually printed here, so nothing on this page should be attributed to a speaker beyond the chair. Typographic oddity: the dateline prints a double space ('18 de mayo de  2005'), and the same double space appears inside each dispatch paragraph at 'proyecto de declaración  de la señora senadora Giusti'; I collapsed it in first_words.
